name: Template base
summary: The smallest working base: a parallel taxiway, one stub, a taxilane, a two-spot apron, one revetment bay, one hangar and the tower. Copy this folder, rename it, and change the numbers.
frame: Metres, in the frame of the world's runway number `runway` (Terrain.runways()). `along` is from the runway's middle towards its far end; the strings "threshold" and "far_end" name its ends, and may carry a signed offset ("threshold+20"), so a longer runway moves what is laid off its ends. `across` is from its centreline, positive to the right looking along it; "runway_edge" is half its width. Heights are from the runway's level. A taxiway is a centreline: one of `along` and `across` is a pair (where it runs) and the other one number (where it lies); its width is `standards.taxiway_width`.

sources.apron_craft: Not a published figure: the widest craft the aprons and taxilanes are laid out for, from the shape table. The plan spaces an apron's spots its span plus wingtip_to_wingtip apart, and stands a revetment block's front its half span plus wingtip_to_taxilane off the taxilane it names, on the side away from the runway (world/airbase_plan.gd, lay).
sources.runway_clear_zone: UFC 3-260-01 (17 Nov 2008) Table 3-2 item 12 and remark 3: Class B runway lateral clearance zone, 1,000 ft from the centreline; a parallel taxiway's pavement lies outside it. https://buildingcriteria1.tpub.com/ufc_3_260_01/index.htm (public domain)
sources.taxiway_width: UFC 3-260-01 Table 5-1 item 1: USAF taxiway 75 ft.
sources.taxiway_obstacle_clearance: UFC 3-260-01 Table 5-1 item 10: taxiway centreline to fixed or mobile obstacles, 200 ft (Air Force).
sources.taxiway_to_taxilane: UFC 3-260-01 Table 5-1 item 11: taxiway centreline to a parallel taxilane, 237.5 ft.
sources.hold_bar: UFC 3-260-01 Table 3-2 item 16: the mandatory frangibility zone, 500 ft wide centred on the runway; the hold bar is at its edge.
sources.wingtip_to_wingtip: UFC 3-260-01 Table 6-1 item 4: parked wingtip to wingtip, 10 ft (spans to 110 ft).
sources.wingtip_to_taxilane: UFC 3-260-01 Table 6-1 item 6: wingtip clearance to a through taxilane, 30 ft.
sources.wall_clearance: AFMAN facility sheet 211111 (Hangar, Aircraft Maintenance) Table 1.2: 10 ft from wingtip or fuselage to walls and doors. https://www.wbdg.org/FFC/AF/AFMAN/211111_Hangar_Maint.pdf (public domain)
sources.revetment_wall_height: AFCESA history of Vietnam-era steel bin revetments: walls 12 ft high at Bien Hoa. https://d34w7g4gy10iej.cloudfront.net/pubs/pdf_75328.pdf (public domain)
sources.revetment_wall_thickness: The same history: bin walls 5.5 ft wide.
sources.sightline_degrees: FAA Order 6480.4A, Airport Traffic Control Tower Siting Criteria: every line of sight meets the surface at 0.80 degrees or steeper (the military rule, UFC 3-260-01 Attachment 18, is 35 arc-minutes). https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Order/ND/6480_4A.pdf (public domain)
sources.hangar_types: UFC 4-211-01 (2017, change 3) Table 7-1, Navy standard hangar modules: Type I 212 x 95 ft, 32.5 ft clear, door 209 x 25 ft; Type III 165 x 165 ft, 50 ft clear, door 162 x 50 ft. https://nibs-s3-wbdg3-production.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/FFC/DOD/UFC/ufc_4_211_01_2017_c3.pdf (public domain)
sources.layout: Kunsan AB (RKJK), Korean AIP AD 2 and its aerodrome chart (facts only): one runway, 2,745 x 45 m; one parallel taxiway on the east with stubs A to E; the main apron between the middle stubs; the tower north-east of the apron. https://aim.koca.go.kr/eaipPub/Package/2024-09-19/html/eAIP/KR-AD-2.RKJK-en-GB.html. Where the revetments stand is this layout's own reading of a typical base: no public plan of Kunsan's shelters was found.
sources.fillet: Not a published figure: the pavement added round a junction on every side, chosen so a fighter turned at its desk-key taxi speed stays on the pavement, and measured by tests/airbase.gd.
